item.title: Model Checking for Noisy Toric Words
item.description: arXiv:2610.23463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Toric words have recently gained attention as a means to model the behaviour of dynamical systems such as linear loops. This work is concerned with describing when the toric model is precise enough to decide whether the trace of a system is contained in an omega-regular language. Our contributions are threefold. (i) We use topological means to generalise a class of toric words by defining noise-robust dynamical systems and their sets of noisy traces. We prove that all noisy traces of a system are almost-periodic, and have the same set of recurrent factors. (ii) We apply the abstract techniques above to concrete sequences obtained as sign descriptions of real algebraic linear recurrence sequences (LRS), and show that the language-membership problem for sign descriptions of LRS with few dominant roots is decidable. (iii) We show that noisy traces of noise-robust dynamical systems are indistinguishable to a prefix-independent omega-regular language, and inclusion is decidable provided the common language of their recurrent factors is recursive. We incidentally obtain properties of prefix-independent omega-regular languages that may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Vahanwala

item.title: Symmetric two-counter machines
item.description: arXiv:2610.23495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counter machines are a particularly simple, Turing-complete model of computation. We study the expressive power of nondeterministic 2-counter machines which are symmetric, in that their set of update transitions is invariant under swapping of counters. Our model is an extension of symmetric 2-VASS, in that we allow modifying both counters within a single transition. As the main result we demonstrate a dramatic impact of symmetry: we show that symmetric 2-counter machines are not Turing-complete, by proving decidability of their reachability problem. We conjecture that the decidability extends to machines with 3 or more counters that are symmetric, meaning the set of update transitions is invariant under any permutation of counters. We leave this problem open for machines with 3 and more counters, while identifying a frontier of the impact of symmetry: we prove undecidability for 3-counter machines invariant under the cyclic permutation group of order 3.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Jaros, {\L}ukasz Kami\'nski, Maja K\k{a}dzio{\l}ka, S{\l}awomir Lasota

item.title: Integer Reachability in Data VASS
item.description: arXiv:2610.23725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data Petri nets are an extension of plain Petri nets where, intuitively speaking, tokens carry data values, and transitions may perform equality tests on data values involved. Likewise, data vector addition systems with states (data VASS) are an extension of plain VASS, and equivalent to data Petri nets. The decidability status of the reachability problem in this model is an established and long-standing open question. In this paper we perform a major step towards resolving this question: we show decidability of the integer reachability problem, where the counters can drop below zero. Contrarily to plain VASS, where integer reachability reduces to integer linear programming, the setting of data VASS is significantly more complex, mostly due to the fact that the state spaces are not finite but orbit-finite (like in register automata). Our decision procedure combines an iterative refinement, resembling the KLM decomposition in plain VASS, with a termination argument via a novel way of bounding the number of data values appearing in the refinement. As corollaries, we deduce decidability of a number of decision problems concerning register automata and data Petri nets.
item.dc:creator: Roland Guttenberg, {\L}ukasz Kami\'nski, S{\l}awomir Lasota

item.title: At the Limits of Computability: Steps Towards Autonomous AI Discovery on the Busy Beaver Frontier
item.description: arXiv:2610.22603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in AI for mathematics---ranging from Olympiad medal performances to resolving long-standing open conjectures---have rapidly expanded what automated systems can achieve. Yet these successes primarily concern predefined, human-formulated problems, leaving open how AI systems can autonomously uncover mathematical structure and formulate new questions. To push beyond static challenges, we explore the Busy Beaver (BB) domain, an uncomputable frontier that is fundamentally open-ended. Because no algorithm can compute the Busy Beaver number $\mathrm{BB}(n)$ for every $n$, this domain provides a natural setting for sustained exploration through mathematical conjecture and proof. In this paper, we introduce a Gemini-based agentic pipeline that automatically discovers accelerations of Turing machines, expressed as compact mathematical rules summarizing many execution steps. Our system integrates pattern recognition, automated conjecturing, informal mathematical reasoning, and formal theorem proving in Lean. With this framework, our system autonomously discovered and formally verified novel Collatz-like accelerations for eleven machines in $\mathrm{BB}(6)$. Subject to community acceptance, we provisionally classify these machines as Cryptids, namely machines whose blank-tape executions admit exact, compact mathematical descriptions but whose halting behavior remains unresolved. These results advance the analysis of $\mathrm{BB}(6)$ holdouts on the Busy Beaver frontier and demonstrate the potential of autonomous AI systems for open-ended mathematical discovery in fundamental computer science.
item.dc:creator: Marco Dos Santos, Vivek Veeriah, Alex Havrilla, Andrew Bolt, Goran Zuzic, Satinder Singh, Tom Zahavy

item.title: Rational decomposition of polyhedra and a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer
item.description: arXiv:2610.22663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove in the affirmative a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer (2003), which relates unambiguous rational sets to a well known result due to Khovanskii and Pukhlikov (1992) and independently to Lawrence (1990) on the valuations of the algebra spanned by the indicator functions of polyhedra.
item.dc:creator: Flavio D'Alessandro, Paolo Papi

item.title: Counting and Sampling Manufacturable Stacking Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.23146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Designing the stacking sequence of a composite laminate is a discrete optimisation problem: each ply takes one of a few orientations, each evaluation may cost a finite-element solve, and the design must obey manufacturing rules and design guidelines, which optimisers enforce by penalty, repair or rejection. We describe the admissible set exactly. The two manufacturing rules forbid a finite set of factors, so the sequences they admit form a regular language, recognised by an automaton that tracks the last orientation and the length of its run; balance and the ten per cent rule constrain the Parikh vector and are carried by a dynamic program over automaton state and counters. One table, polynomial in N, counts the admissible sequences without producing them, draws them uniformly, and tells whether a partial sequence can still be completed. We give pseudocode, exact counts for three orientation sets, closed-form ceilings on the composition, and four of the five single-rule entries a published table left uncomputed. At 48 plies, 99.8% of the nodes of a layer-wise search tree checking the rules locally have no admissible completion on eight orientations; the completion test removes them. A one-point crossover that cuts two admissible parents only where they share an automaton state and their child closes the counters returns admissible children by construction.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Langiu, Felice Rubino, Giacomo Canale

item.title: Complexity of liveness in ring Petri nets and of halting in chip-firing on simple digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A ring Petri net (weighted circuit, cyclic weighted T-system) consists of a single directed circuit with arbitrary positive arc weights. We show that deciding liveness of ring Petri nets is coNP-complete, and that coNP-hardness holds in the strong sense already for token-conserving rings, in which every transition consumes and produces the same number of tokens. The proof is a short reduction from the covering problem for systems of residue classes (the complement of Simultaneous Incongruences). Together with a known reduction to circuits, it follows that liveness of weighted T-systems (weighted marked graphs, synchronous dataflow graphs) is coNP-complete, and coNP-hard in the strong sense. As a further consequence, the halting problem for chip-firing on simple directed graphs is NP-complete, which answers a question of Farrell and Levine. On 7 October 2026, the problem of liveness was posed to the AI model Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), which found the reduction, also suggesting the application to the chip-firing problem, and wrote a first version of this paper; the human authors checked it and, together with the model, revised it iteratively into the present form.
item.dc:creator: Eike Best, Raymond Devillers, Petr Jan\v{c}ar, Mat\v{e}j O\v{s}\v{t}\'{a}dal
